title: searchfor match data
description: The `data` object of a `match` message of `sfor --json`. ripgrep's own fields (path, lines, line_number, absolute_offset, submatches) keep ripgrep's meaning and are not constrained here beyond what searchfor adds to them. Added field names are stable from v0.1: new fields may appear, existing ones are never renamed.

format.description: Name of the file's Format ("markdown", "yaml", "php"…), or null for Plain files and for files whose Processor is unavailable or failed.

trail.description: Trail of the line's first submatch (of the line start for an inverted match): the Segments from the root of the file down to the Match. Empty for Plain files and for Matches at the top level.

fragment.description: null when the line fits in --fragment-width; otherwise the line's first Fragment.

section.description: Only with --expand: the Section of the last Segment of `trail`, or null when the Trail is empty.

trail.description: Present on every submatch when the submatches of the line have different Trails (two cells of one table row).

section.description: Only with --expand, on a submatch whose Section differs from the line's `section`.

kind.description: A free string, never an enumeration. Markdown: document, heading, code, item, column. YAML, JSON and TOML (from v0.2): key, element, and document for the documents of a YAML stream. Code (from v0.2): the `kinds` of the Format Definition, such as class, method, function, namespace, struct, impl, or the tree-sitter node kind when `kinds` has none. Helper Processors and later Formats add kinds.

line.description: 1-based first line of the Segment's Section.

end_line.description: 1-based last line of the Section, inclusive.

signature.description: The line that declares the Segment, for code (from v0.2).

start.description: Byte offset of `text` in the line.

text.description: Lines start_line..=end_line of the file, line terminators included.
